svg.title: A journey with room to spare

text.tspan: Travelers look at a map to consider their route.
A journey with room to spare
When we plan a short trip, a little care can make the experience better. Planning and thinking
First, checking the route reduces avoidable confusion. For example, we write down the platform
and the time of the last train. This is a small thing that makes the day easier.
Second, leaving spare time makes changes easier to manage. For example, we choose an
earlier bus rather than risk missing our connection. We do not need a perfect day to do this well.
We can plan a short trip more easily when we prepare and notice other people. These simple
steps give us a useful place to start.
BUILD YOUR OWN · State a focused main idea. Develop one supporting reason in each body paragraph, with a concrete
example. Conclude by connecting the two reasons without introducing a new argument. Use the structure as a model; write
about an experience of your own.
Tell a friend. What two reasons support the main idea? Explain one example. (Model: The two reasons are that checking the
route reduces avoidable confusion and that leaving spare time makes changes easier to manage. One example is that we
write down the platform and the time of the last train.)
